case_title: Om Prakash v. Union of India & Ors.
accused_victim_relationship: Co-worker: both served in the same army unit; the judgment describes no prior enmity beyond the farewell-party altercation
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 (charged); IPC s.304 Part II (conviction), with s.34 referred to in the headnote
evidence_type: Circumstantial evidence; eyewitness-type testimony about the room and departure; medical evidence; recorded statement under Rule 23 of the Army Rules
confession: Police-station confession to Army officers: not relied on. Statement recorded under Rule 23 (Exh. 36): relied on as voluntary and proved
aggravating_circumstances: Altercation at party; drunken state; alone in room with deceased; left by rear door; presence at police station at odd hour; absence from fall-in parade
trial_court_outcome: General Court Martial convicted under IPC s.304 Part II (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and sentenced to 7 years rigorous imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Writ petition in Delhi High Court transferred to Armed Forces Tribunal, which treated it as an appeal under s.15; no separate High Court decision on merits stated
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder, IPC s.304 Part II
neutral_facts: At a farewell party at an army unit's barracks, drinks were served. The accused became involved in a heated argument with a senior non-commissioned officer, who slapped the accused. The accused then fought with and abused that officer and also abused the victim, a fellow soldier, who had tried to intervene. An officer intervened and directed two junior soldiers to escort the accused to his living barracks. Later, the victim was found lying on the floor of the room, bleeding from the mouth and nose, with a stab wound to the chest. The accused was found lying on a bed in the same room. Witnesses testified that no one other than the accused and the victim had been present in the room, and that the accused had been seen leaving quietly through the rear door. The accused was absent from the morning fall-in parade. At about 1.30 to 2 a.m., the accused surrendered at a nearby police station and said he had stabbed a person with a knife. Unit officers went to the station, and the accused confessed to stabbing the victim. The forensic surgeon who conducted the autopsy found two ante mortem injuries, one a deep stab wound to the chest that could have caused death. The knife was not recovered. A statement the accused gave during a summary of evidence under the army rules, describing a scuffle and saying he stabbed the victim to free his neck, was proved through the officer who recorded it, with a supporting witness. The adjutant lodged an FIR and the accused was handed to military police.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from a stab wound to the chest (3 x 2 cm, deep to chest cavity); a second injury was a linear abrasion on the back of the chest
number_of_offences: 1 charged (IPC s.302); 1 finally upheld (IPC s.304 Part II)
premeditation_planning: Not found. The GCM found no intention to kill but knowledge that death was a likely consequence; the Supreme Court did not address premeditation
motive: alleged: altercation and quarrel at the farewell party while intoxicated, with the victim intervening
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony that only the accused and the victim were in the room; that the accused left by the rear door; that the accused was absent from the fall-in parade; surrender at the police station; autopsy evidence of a knife wound; the Rule 23 statement (Exh. 36) proved through PW30 and corroborated by CW2
witness_credibility: Minor discrepancies did not damage the testimony; the witnesses stood firm under roving cross-examination; the evidence read in entirety was found reliable
post_offence_conduct: Left the room quietly by the rear door; was absent from the fall-in parade; surrendered at the police station around 1.30 to 2 a.m. and disclosed the stabbing to officers; gave no explanation for his presence there
trial_duration: offence: 3 April 2006; trial judgment: GCM order dated 24.2.2007; High Court: not given (writ W.P.(C) No.7266 of 2009 transferred to AFT); Supreme Court: July 09, 2015
legal_representation: Accused/appellant: Mohit Kumar Shah. Respondents (Union of India): R. Balasubramaniam, Amarendra Bal, Vikas Malhotra, B.V. Bairam Das and Anil Katiyar
investigation_status: FIR lodged by the adjutant; accused handed to military police; GCM proceedings initiated; 31 prosecution witnesses examined
appeal_history: Trial (GCM, 24.2.2007): convicted under s.304 Part II, 7 years RI. High Court: writ transferred to Armed Forces Tribunal. Armed Forces Tribunal (TA 617/2009, 05.04.2010): conviction and sentence affirmed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: Ample material established the chain of circumstantial evidence; minor discrepancies did not matter; non-recovery of the knife was immaterial; the Rule 23 statement was corroborated; the accused's petition under s.164 admitted use of a knife in self-defence
defence_argument: The police-station confession was inadmissible; the Rule 23 statement was legally unsound; discrepancies and hearsay undermined the evidence; the knife was not recovered; others were present in the room; presence was doubtful; relied on Ravindran and Rumi Bora Dutta
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence must form a complete chain consistent only with guilt, and the circumstances must be conclusive; a statement under Rule 23 is admissible if voluntary and made with statutory safeguards
precedent_relied_upon: Hema v. State (2013) 10 SCC 192; Union of India v. Major Rabinder Singh (2012) 12 SCC 787; Appabhai v. State of Gujarat AIR 1988 SC 696; Rohtash Kumar v. State of Haryana (2013) 14 SCC 434; Bachan Singh v. Union of India (2008) 9 SCC 161; referred: Gilbert Pereira (2004) 12 SCC 281, Ravindran (2007) 6 SCC 410, Rumi Bora Dutta (2013) 7 SCC 417
